market_note: No names enter or exit; the only roster change is GOOGL moving ahead of AAPL (Alphabet's market cap now exceeds Apple's, #2 vs #3, with stronger AI/cloud momentum), so order is NVDA, GOOGL, AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, META, TSLA, BRK-B, LLY, WMT. Tone was risk-off into the week: Warsh's debut FOMC was a hawkish hold (3.50-3.75%, 9 of 18 dots now pencil a 2026 hike, easing bias dropped) that knocked the Nasdaq ~1.3% on Jun 17, even as NVDA priced a record 3x-oversubscribed $25B bond and held near all-time highs and an ~$3.6T AI-IPO pipeline (SpaceX's record IPO, Cursor buyout) stokes both enthusiasm and supply fears.

names.name: NVIDIA
names.driver: Blackwell-led data-center demand drove record Q1 FY27 revenue and a record 3x-oversubscribed $25B bond to fund AI infrastructure, with the stock near all-time highs and a ~$5T cap.
names.risk: Extreme expectations leave it priced for perfection, so any China-export, hyperscaler-capex-digestion, or AI-bubble wobble hits hardest in a hawkish-Fed tape.
names.guide: Management guided Q2 FY27 revenue to ~$91B, well above consensus, signaling continued near-doubling of data-center sales.
names.cash: Raised dividend ~25x; funding capex via record $25B IG bond

names.name: Alphabet
names.driver: Google Cloud revenue accelerated to +63% YoY with backlog near $460B and Gemini/enterprise AI now the primary cloud growth driver, lifting Alphabet past Apple to #2 by market cap.
names.risk: Search-ad disruption from AI answers plus a $180-190B capex bill and antitrust overhang could compress margins if monetization lags.
names.guide: Management raised 2026 capex to $180-190B and framed AI as accelerating both cloud and search monetization.
names.cash: EPS +82% YoY; ongoing large buyback and dividend

names.name: Apple
names.driver: Record March-quarter revenue with iPhone +22% and Services at an all-time high drove a guide far above consensus, plus a fresh $100B buyback authorization.
names.risk: A memory-chip shortage and higher component costs threaten margins, and Apple still lacks a clear frontier-AI catalyst versus peers.
names.guide: Management guided fiscal Q3 to 14-17% revenue growth, far above the ~9.5% Street view, but flagged supply constraints.

names.name: Microsoft
names.driver: Azure grew ~40% and the AI business cleared a $37B run-rate (+123% YoY) with Copilot past 20M seats, beating on both revenue and EPS.
names.risk: Capacity remains tight and the heavy AI capex cycle pressures free cash flow if cloud demand or monetization decelerates under higher rates.
names.guide: Management signaled continued strong double-digit cloud growth with Azure capacity constraints easing over coming quarters.
names.cash: Robust FCF funding capex; steady dividend and buyback

names.name: Amazon
names.driver: AWS reaccelerated to +28% (15-quarter high, ~$150B run-rate) while retail margins expanded and ads grew +24%, beating the high end of guidance.
names.risk: Capex surged to ~$44B/quarter for AI buildout, so any AWS deceleration or consumer-spend softening in a hawkish-Fed environment squeezes margins.
names.guide: Management guided Q2 to $194-199B net sales (16-19% growth) with operating income above consensus.
names.cash: Strong operating cash flow funding ~$44B/qtr capex; no dividend

names.name: Meta Platforms
names.driver: Ad revenue grew +33% with AI tools lifting conversion, net income +61%, as Superintelligence Labs shipped its first model.
names.risk: 2026 capex raised to $125-145B with expenses up sharply, so investors may punish the spend if AI returns stay unproven (stock already fell on the capex raise).
names.guide: Management lifted full-year capex and expense outlooks, signaling an aggressive multi-year AI investment cycle.
names.cash: $81B cash; FCF $12.4B; buyback and dividend active

names.name: Tesla
names.driver: Robotaxi expanded to Dallas and Houston (now three live cities), FSD subscriptions jumped +51% to 1.28M, and surprise positive FCF supported the AI/autonomy narrative.
names.risk: Core auto growth has stalled (deliveries missed) and a rich AI/robotaxi-driven valuation is highly rate-sensitive and execution-dependent.
names.guide: Management is pushing robotaxi to several new metros, framing autonomy and AI as the primary value driver over autos.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: $22.4B, +16% YoY, mixed (EPS beat, deliveries missed)
names.backlog: Order backlog modest; robotaxi rollout pipeline in multiple cities
names.cash: FCF positive $1.4B; large cash balance; no dividend

names.name: Berkshire Hathaway
names.driver: Operating earnings rose 18% in Greg Abel's first quarter as CEO, with a record ~$397B cash pile offering defensive optionality and buyback firepower.
names.risk: The record cash hoard reflects a dearth of attractive deals, and a defensive, low-AI-beta name can lag a momentum-driven, tech-led tape.
names.guide: Abel signaled continued discipline, deploying capital opportunistically while the cash buffer cushions a hawkish macro.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: operating earnings $11.35B, +18% YoY, slight miss (vs $11.56B est)
names.cash: Record ~$397B cash; opportunistic buybacks; no dividend

names.name: Eli Lilly
names.driver: GLP-1 franchise surged with Mounjaro sales doubling and oral orforglipron (Foundayo) launching, prompting a raise to full-year guidance.
names.risk: GLP-1 pricing pressure, intensifying competition, and supply/scaling execution could temper the rich growth multiple.
names.guide: Management raised 2026 revenue guidance to $82-85B and non-GAAP EPS to $35.50-37.00 on new-medicine momentum.
names.cash: Strong cash generation funding capacity expansion and dividend

names.name: Walmart
names.driver: US comps +4.1% and global e-commerce +26% (led by delivery, advertising, marketplace) drove a revenue beat with high-margin streams scaling.
names.risk: Higher fuel/distribution costs pressured operating margin, and a defensive staple offers limited upside if risk appetite stays AI-tech-led.
names.guide: Management guided Q2 to 4-5% sales growth and 7-10% adjusted operating-income growth, with full-year outlook unchanged.
names.cash: Steady FCF; consistent dividend and buyback
